angle: While other p-value sources define and move on, this video drills one explicit three-part recipe (observed plus equally rare plus rarer-or-more-extreme) across tiny coin enumerations and then a continuous height distribution, ending with a worked warning against one-sided p-values.
angle_detail: Learn the recipe at [04:49]-[09:12] via the two-flip p-value of 0.5 and its flower analogy, then transfer it at [13:08]-[20:09] to tail areas: 142 cm borderline, 141 cm significant, near-mean probability small yet p-value 1. Finish with the one-sided trap from [22:01], where a drug that worsens recovery scores 0.98 one-sided versus 0.03 two-sided. No named test statistic appears, so bridge to z/t procedures separately.
